item.title: Manage Your Account
item.description:
Your profile belongs to you, not to an organization. A change applies in every organization you belong to. This guide covers the four things you can change about your account: the profile, the password, the linked sign-in providers, and the account itself.

Before you start 🔗

  • You need the View Profile permission to open the profile. The default user role holds it.
  • Changing your password needs Reset Password. Deleting the account needs Delete Account. The default user role holds both.
  • Layer5 Cloud signs you in through an identity service. Password changes and account deletion need a live browser sign-in. A script that holds only an API token cannot do either.
  • Changing a password or linking a provider is a privileged action. If your sign-in is older than the privileged-session window, Layer5 Cloud asks you to sign in again first. The window is 24 hours on hosted Layer5 Cloud and 15 minutes by default in the self-hosted chart.
  • A user’s profile can also be edited by an administrator who holds Update User Profile in an organization you share with them. Only a Provider Admin can change another user’s email address.

Edit your profile 🔗

The profile form saves itself. About one second after you stop typing, Layer5 Cloud saves the change and confirms it with a short message. There is no Save button, and edits made during a save are queued, not lost.

item.title: Your Account
item.description:
Your account is your identity across every organization you belong to. These guides cover the settings that belong to you, and the subscription that belongs to the organization you administer. For how accounts relate to organizations, sign-in methods, and roles, read the Users concept.

The account area has four tabs: Profile, Preferences, Subscription, and Plans. Each tab opens only for a user who holds its permission. Without the permission, the tab shows a permission-denied view.

item.title: Recognize Members with Badges
item.description:
A recognition is a badge that an organization defines and awards to its members. Recognitions mark milestones such as completing training, contributing to a project, or reaching a team goal. An awarded badge appears on the recipient’s public profile, where the recipient can share it.

Two kinds of badges exist, and they come from different places:

  • Organization recognitions are created and awarded by an organization’s administrators. This guide covers them.
  • Layer5 community badges belong to the Layer5 community recognition program. Browse them in the Badge Gallery and read how they are earned in the Recognition section of the Layer5 Community Handbook.

Who can do what 🔗

Task What it needs
Create, edit, or delete a recognition The Manage Recognitions permission in the organization that owns the recognition. Organization Admin, Provider Admin, and Academy Admin hold it by default. The Manage Recognitions control on the Organizations page is enabled for holders of Edit Organization.
Award a recognition to a member The permission to update that member’s profile, held in an organization you share with the member.
View a badge Anyone who can open the recipient’s public profile.
